title: Engine::locate stops at the repository boundary and repo-root is the first candidate
action: Review B-P2-3: Engine::locate walks cwd to / with no boundary — the nearest ancestor carrying packages/bee/AGENTS.block.md becomes the vendoring source (template/hook poisoning), and the repo-root flag is never a candidate (INSTALL.md's 'from any terminal' is false). Fix: (1) the upward walk STOPS after the first directory containing .git (file or dir — the repository boundary): inside a repo only that repo can win; outside any repo the walk keeps today's behavior to the filesystem root. (2) When the caller passed the repo-root flag, that root is tried FIRST as a locate candidate (its own packages/bee/AGENTS.block.md); only on miss does the cwd walk run, and LocateError then names both candidates. (3) Tests: neutralize ambient BEE_JS_ENTRY with a scoped env guard in every locate test; pin PRODUCTION Engine::locate() behavior — red test: ancestor ABOVE a .git boundary carries templates, cwd inside the repo without templates -> refusal (old code: ancestor wins); repo-root candidate test: cwd elsewhere, repo-root at a real checkout -> engine resolves. Existing onboard tests stay green (they use run_with_root and bypass locate).

truths: an ancestor beyond the repo's .git boundary can never become the template source
onboard with the repo-root flag at a bee checkout works from any cwd
locate tests are immune to ambient BEE_JS_ENTRY

artifacts.substantive: bounded walk + repo-root candidate plus tests

trace.outcome: locate walk stops at first .git boundary; repo-root is first candidate and LocateError names both; BEE_JS_ENTRY neutralized in tests; locate() pure delegate pinned via locate_from
